answer: An anti-sybil bonding curve charges each operator a bond that rises quadratically with the identities it controls. The ledger links wallets by their attestation graph, so a farm's clones count as one operator and the Nth identity costs N squared times the base. A zephyr of cheap wallets is far from free: a hundred clones costs ten thousand times more. Solo users stay near zero. A bridge of shared keys or coordinated signing exposes the cluster and triggers the curve. The only safe reef is one genuine identity; the attacker pays N squared bonds plus real work per wallet, not one fixed deposit.
